ontology.note: Emits an fw:ConvexHull activity carrying fw:recordCount, fw:hullVertexCount, fw:hullAreaSquareMetres, fw:hullSpanMetres and fw:metricCRS, and prov:used the point source. The area and span are emitted rather than a threshold applied: points lying on one meridian are collinear in degrees and not in metres, so they yield a correct hull of a few square metres spanning kilometres, and a cutoff would also refuse a genuinely thin distribution.

changes.description: Show me how it works, in Configure…: Six made-up cases: the band caught on the outermost, the one inside that does not shape it, and the outline the step makes with its area and widest span.

evidence.note: Seven unit checks cover the monotone chain keeping corners and dropping interior and on-edge points; refusal of two points, of duplicates and of collinear input; refusal of a layer with fewer than three located points, naming how many it had; unlocated records taking no part and being reported; computation in a projected CRS with coordinates returned as longitude and latitude; the stated area and span for a near-collinear layer, measured at 3.6 square metres across 2,225 metres; and the limitation travelling in both the notes and the receipt. Not established: that a hull is the right boundary for anything. It is the smallest convex one, which is a mathematical property and not a claim that the phenomenon is convex. 0.3.0: tests/spatial-walkthroughs.browser.mjs, Show me how stepped to its last sentence; Chromium, 2026-11-23.
